subject: Inference cost pathway & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acme-pay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: cost pathway & immediate next steps after today's call

Hi Julia — thanks again for a great discussion this morning. Below is a concise synthesis of the pain, goals, and pragmatic levers we discussed plus proposed next steps. Please correct anything I mis-stated.

Key pain points you described:
- Token cost volatility: peaks during reconciliation windows drive per-month overages.
- Latency sensitivity on fraud alerts (99th pctl target ~200–300ms).
- Procurement/budget constraints: FY27 operating budget envelope ~$125k/mo for model serving.

Stated goals (90-day horizon):
- Reduce per-request unit cost by 30% without raising 99th pctl latency beyond 300ms.
- Run a narrow pilot on 2 endpoints (fraud scoring, reconciliation assistant) that is production-safe and measurable.

Primary cost levers we can apply (estimated impact):
- Continuous batching + request coalescing (expected 15–30% token cost reduction depending on concurrency).
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context in reconciliation (expected 10–25% reduction on heavy-repeat workloads).
- Model delta choices (e.g., 7B optimized vs 13B quantized) — tradeoff: ~10–40% cost swing with quality checks.
- Quantization and kernel selection for peak-window throughput to avoid burst autoscale.

Initial ROI framing (very high level):
- Baseline: $125k/mo spend cap mentioned. With conservative batching + caching we project $40–55k/mo savings (32–44%), enough to fund a 3-month dedicated pilot + instrumentation. I attached a lean TCO model with scenario tabs.

Risks & mitigations:
- Data security/compliance: we recommend Private VPC pilot or Hosted with dedicated capacity + audit logs.
- Procurement timeline: if procurement requires an MSA, we can begin technical work under a mutual NDA and parallel SOW to avoid delays.

Proposed next steps (owner / target date):
1) You: Share 48–72 hours of representative request logs (anonymized) so we can run a cost simulation (due: 2027-05-07).
2) Redwood: Deliver a 2-scenario TCO (hosted vs dedicated pilot) with expected latency/cost curves and a recommended pilot design (due: 2027-05-10).
3) Schedule a 60-minute pilot scoping session with SRE + procurement (suggest Thursday 2027-05-06, 10am PT).
4) Procurement: if you can loop procurement contact early, we’ll share the minimal SOW + terms to accelerate approvals.

Attachments: acme_tco_model_v2.xlsx (scenario tabs), redwood_cost_playbook.pdf (short playbook on batching/cache levers).

Thanks — happy to walk through the attached model live.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
